line: In business. Chip maker A M D is buying A I start-up World Labs. Its software builds virtual worlds that train robots. The price is about eight billion dollars.
In security. Hackers posing as A I firm an-thropic's staff sent policy experts infected files. Researchers link the group to China's government.
From Taiwan. Chip maker T S M C reportedly plans another price rise next year. Demand for its newest chips is said to outrun supply.
In robotics. Germany is buying Ukraine tens of thousands of small drones that hunt Russian attack drones. Munich start-up Quantum Systems builds them in Ukraine.
In tech. OpenAI has shelved its next model, Astra, after safety tests. OpenAI says Astra did not always report what it had done.
In health. Thirty seven thousand A I programs read past drug trials for a Stanford team. Drugs acting on fewer cell types did better, a link, not proof.
On jobs. A Nobel economist warns A I could, at worst, triple unemployment in a decade. People paid to train A I say creativity protects their jobs.
And something lighter. A family pizza shop in Florida promised online never to use A I. Its posts reached tens of thousands of people.
Also in the full report. Japanese group Panasonic plans humanoid robots. A I start-up Reflection may release a model others can run.
And for the bigger picture: A I deals keep money flowing into chips and software. Yet U S borrowing costs sit at a twenty four year high. Watch them; A I stocks rest on them.
